svg.aria-label: Cluster topology: symmetric query nodes over one shared bucket, with remote clusters reached only through their API
svg.text: Clients (PromQL / SQL / Flight SQL)
query node A -- coordinator
mode all|query, --distributed-query
resolves ONE pinned snapshot
partitions, dispatches, merges
serves SeriesFetch + Flight SQL
query node B -- peer worker
same binary, same flags: any node is a
coordinator for the requests it receives
and a worker for its peers' slices
fragment surface on --listen-grpc only
A and B exchange slices in either direction over the cluster-internal gRPC listener, bearer-token authed.
S3 bucket = one cluster (the only durable state)
immutable segments, commit records, manifests, snapshot HEAD/parts
sys/gc, sys/tenancy, sys/query/workers/<process_id> heartbeats
Membership: every distributed query node PUTs its own sys/query/workers/<process_id> record every
60 s; readers take the live set as records within 3 x H and rendezvous-hash (tenant_hash, signal, shard).
reached only through their own API
Remote Ravel clusters (--remote-cluster): separate buckets, separate trust domains
Reached only through the remote's own API endpoint: the coordinator sends matchers and a window,
the remote resolves its own snapshot under its own operator credential and its own erasure.
No segment references, no S3 credentials, and no client credential ever cross this boundary.
Compute stays disposable: a node can be added or removed at any time, and membership reconverges.
